questions.question_en: An alcohol X (C₅H₁₂O) produces turbidity instantly with conc. HCl/ZnCl₂. Isomer (Y) of X undergoes dehydration with conc. H₂SO₄ at 443 K. X and Y respectively are
options_en: a chain alcohol with OH near one end (branched, primary-looking) ; a tertiary alcohol shape with OH on a quaternary-adjacent carbon
(CH₃)₂C(OH)CH₂CH₃ — 2-methylbutan-2-ol (tertiary, HO– drawn on the left) ; CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂CH₂OH — 3-methylbutan-1-ol (primary alcohol)
questions.note: has diagram; options are skeletal structures of C5H12O alcohol isomers illustrating the Lucas test (conc. HCl/ZnCl2 instant turbidity = tertiary alcohol). The marked-correct option 3 is chemically unambiguous — X = 2-methylbutan-2-ol (tertiary), Y = its isomer 3-methylbutan-2-ol (secondary, consistent with acid-catalysed dehydration). The precise chain/OH position drawn in distractor options 1, 2 and 4 was harder to pin down pixel-exactly from the crop and is transcribed to the best of visual judgement.
